brief.markdown:
# Election update: Wednesday, November 4 (evening)

## Bottom line
The House results table now shows Democrats past a majority: 375 of 435 races are marked called, D 235 and R 140. Majority is 218 ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)). Counting 4 more races news outlets report as called, it is D 237, R 142. In the Senate, Democrats have secured 54 seats to Republicans' 44, counting seats not up ([Senate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Mississippi and Alaska are uncalled; the BBC reports Mississippi is separated by dozens of votes ([BBC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTE1HMzQwZkNtWnM3ci1XOWpTeGItSFhoVzUtdGVENE1jZkFDVnFuUzVycjJuSnNUUWNxVzVralZfRkJZcWZvTjhJQnVGMUNiMndIRmQyRzVNczZmVm8?oc=5)). CNBC recaps the result as Democrats flipping both chambers ([CNBC](https://news.google.?oc=5)).

## Called since the last update
- **Competitive House flips since this morning (11):** CA-22 (Randy Villegas, D), MI-04 (Sean McCann, D), MI-07 (William Lawrence, D), MI-10 (Christina Hines, D), MT-01 (Sam Forstag, D), NY-17 (Cait Conley, D), OH-07 (Brian Poindexter, D), OH-15 (Don Leonard, D), VA-02 (Elaine Luria, D), WI-01 (Mitchell Berman, D), WI-03 (Rebecca Cooke, D) ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)).
- **Competitive House holds since this morning (12):** CA-13 (Adam Gray, D), NC-01 (Don Davis, D), NM-02 (Gabe Vasquez, D), NV-01 (Dina Titus, D), NV-03 (Susie Lee, D), NV-04 (Steven Horsford, D), OH-01 (Greg Landsman, D), OH-09 (Marcy Kaptur, D), TX-09 (Leticia Gutierrez, D), TX-28 (Henry Cuellar, D), TX-34 (Vicente Gonzalez, D), TX-35 (Johnny Garcia, D).
- Plus 126 safe or likely seats called as rated. No Senate race was called today.
- **Correction:** the results table no longer marks NC-13 (Barringer) or NC-14 (Womack) as called for Democrats, and it dropped its mark on NC-06. This morning's update listed NC-13 and NC-14 as Democratic wins based on those marks. We now treat all three as uncalled until the table or an AP-attributed report confirms them ([House table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_elections)).

## Still uncalled
Every competitive race not yet marked called in the results table, Senate first. A race news outlets report as called says so with its source; we count those separately until the table follows AP.
- **AK Senate** (Tossup): ranked-choice tabulation and a pending lawsuit could make the decision slow, KCRA reports ([KCRA](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiygFBVV95cUxPUDNfUkFWcmp2dkx4OGYwTXJlVlNQeV9kd05BYzQ5X3lncjJhRlRMRVNtMjZzMVVIU2tOUktHS0hsZXZiZ3lRRnVvbVBOUzRCcjhLQzJFSGRJTU0zeUdFNWowam1iX1FEZlBqajRqb1lHdWRTNkMzcHloQWlRSTlEdWtVek1XOW1XR2l5WFB2SkxhUG9nYTM3VWVSTmYwalZUQmtzeVc5ckhwRmdLVG1QNFgxZ1B2LXBCNEw3aU5mZks0b2xjOWdiYk9B?oc=5)).
- **MS Senate** (Likely R): the BBC reports the Democrat leads by dozens of votes ([BBC](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTE1HMzQwZkNtWnM3ci1XOWpTeGItSFhoVzUtdGVENE1jZkFDVnFuUzVycjJuSnNUUWNxVzVralZfRkJZcWZvTjhJQnVGMUNiMndIRmQyRzVNczZmVm8?oc=5)); Mississippi has no recount law, the NYT reports ([NYT](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiigFBVV95cUxOdVFrTnpfc3UxeXZIWW9CWXNNck1mbGhFR0ZWQ0gzVWxBUFdrSWFPRjlBUjdVMVlpNFdCVi11ZXBMeklRMHRxNThZc3NxeWJyWVJJa3BFMkR3azRvVWI0ZklheU40Uk5XN21BRF9ZM29MaG1ZTWpld1k0UzM3bXNKeWdRZWhHX3ZaRmc?oc=5)).
